Subject: Request: data routing options, subprocessors and DPF evidence

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — Silverline's security and legal team have a few follow-ups for the procurement RFP. We need clear, written confirmation for three items to advance to legal review: (1) a current list of subprocessors and whether any have access to cleartext customer content, (2) routing and residency options (can we force EU-only execution and storage for PHI-derived payloads?) and (3) the specific transfer mechanisms you rely on for EU->US traffic (SCCs, DPF, other).

Could you provide a short technical note and any supporting artifacts (subprocessor CSV, DPA annex language, transfer matrix) by EOD Monday? Legal would also like to know if backups or disaster recovery copies can be restricted to EU regions.

Appreciate it — feel free to loop in product/infra owners.

Best,
Emma Clarke
Director, Procurement
Silverline Healthcare

Date: 2028-03-05T17:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: data routing options, subprocessors and DPF evidence — artifacts attached

Emma / Raj / Legal Ops — attaching the pack we discussed. Summary below; see attachments for CSV and DPA excerpt.

Summary (short):
- Subprocessors: attached CSV (redwood-subprocessor-list-20280304.csv). Primary subprocessors with potential access to decrypted content are: (1) Redwood-managed inference fleet (we are the processor — no third-party access to cleartext unless a customer enables an integration), (2) Cloud storage for logs/backups: AWS EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-west-2) and GCP EU (europe-west4) depending on customer selection, (3) telemetry/observability vendor (Datadog) which receives aggregated metrics by default; logs containing identifiers are only forwarded if the customer enables debug mode — see CSV column "access_level". The CSV includes contact, purpose, and historic SOC/ISO attestations.

- Routing & residency controls: We offer three patterns:
  1) Hosted-default: strong routing policies but multi-region (US + EU) to meet latency. Data may transit US for certain control-plane operations.
  2) EU-Only Hosted: For customers requiring EU-only execution and storage we offer an EU-only tenancy option which pins inference and storage to EU regions and disables cross-border backups by default. This is available on Dedicated or Private plans.
  3) Private/VPC or On-prem: full customer-controlled networking where all egress can be prevented to non-EU endpoints.

- Transfers & legal mechanisms:
  - For Hosted-default customers, outbound transfers are supported by EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs / EDPB-approved text) and our documented DPF mapping where applicable.
  - For Dedicated/Private EU-Only tenancies we can ensure no personal data leaves the EU; where minimal control-plane metadata must route to our control plane, we can provide pseudonymization and a contractual commitment in the DPA annex.

- Backups & DR: Backups are configurable per-customer. For EU-Only tenants and Private deployments we can restrict backups to EU regions and enforce encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK). For Hosted-default customers backups may exist in multiple regions; retention and location are documented in the attached transfer-matrix.

Attached artifacts: redwood-subprocessor-list-20280304.csv (subprocessor registry), dpa-annex-response-silverline-20280304.pdf (clauses and commitment language), transfer-matrix-eu-us-20280304.xlsx (region/backup mapping and control plane notes).

Next steps we suggest:
1) Legal Ops to indicate whether DPF evidence templates are required (we can complete Silverline's standard DPF spreadsheet).
2) If EU-only residency is required for PHI, confirm product plan (Dedicated vs Private) and we'll produce a Statement of Work with environment configuration.

If helpful, Ben and Karthik are available for a technical call Tuesday 03/06 to walk the infra controls.

Regards,
Lauren

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-list-20280304.csv, dpa-annex-response-silverline-20280304.pdf, transfer-matrix-eu-us-20280304.xlsx

Raj — short answers here and we'll add the contractual sentence into the DPA annex draft if you confirm you need it: 

1) Backups & replication guarantee: For EU-Only Hosted tenancies and for Private deployments we can contractually guarantee that primary backups and snapshots will be stored only in EU regions. Third-party cloud provider DR copies (e.g., cross-region replication initiated by the provider) will be disabled in our standard EU-only configuration; we will include a DPA annex clause: "Redwood will not replicate customer backups or snapshots to non-EU jurisdictions for customers electing EU-Only tenancy, except where explicit, documented, and mutually agreed DR scenarios are approved in writing." We can include CMK enforcement and audit logs for snapshot actions.

2) Cleartext access when debug enabled: The only subprocessors that may see cleartext in debug scenarios are our (a) managed infra ops team (Redwood employees) and (b) the optional remote-support vendor listed in the CSV (SupportCo) — which we only enable under customer-approved support sessions. The CSV column "access_level" marks these entries as "debug:conditional" and includes contact/offboarding dates and SOC attestations. For customers with strict confidentiality needs we recommend EU-Only tenancy + Private VPC or an on-prem package.

If you confirm you want the DPA annex sentence we noted above, we'll insert the exact language and re-circulate. Ben, can you confirm the CMK enforcement language and where to reference the audit log entry IDs we will produce? Karthik, can you confirm the default snapshot replication setting for EU-only tenants?

Thanks,
Lauren

Confirmed: CMK enforcement and snapshot-region restrictions are supported for EU-Only tenancies. Audit log entries for snapshot creation, export, and destruction are retained for 1 year (can be extended under SOW). We'll include the specific clause in the DPA annex: "Snapshots and backups for EU-Only tenants will be withheld from non-EU replication. All snapshot lifecycle events will be logged and provided to the customer on request as part of compliance reporting."
